title: Rigveda 10.181: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.181: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.181 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 152r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.181.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 39); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 152r
translation.original_text:
1pratha̍ś ca̱ yasya̍ sa̱pratha̍ś ca̱ nāmānu̍ṣṭubhasya ha̱viṣo̍ ha̱vir yat | dhā̱tur dyutā̍nāt savi̱tuś ca̱ viṣṇo̍ rathaṁta̱ram ā ja̍bhārā̱ vasi̍ṣṭhaḥ ||
2avi̍nda̱n te ati̍hita̱ṁ yad āsī̍d ya̱jñasya̱ dhāma̍ para̱maṁ guhā̱ yat | dhā̱tur dyutā̍nāt savi̱tuś ca̱ viṣṇo̍r bha̱radvā̍jo bṛ̱had ā ca̍kre a̱gneḥ ||
3te̍ 'vinda̱n mana̍sā̱ dīdhyā̍nā̱ yaju̍ḥ ṣka̱nnam pra̍tha̱maṁ de̍va̱yāna̍m | dhā̱tur dyutā̍nāt savi̱tuś ca̱ viṣṇo̱r ā sūryā̍d abharan gha̱rmam e̱te ||
translation.text:
1Vasishṭha mastered the Rathantara, took it from radiant Dhatar, Savitar, and Vishṇu, Oblation, portion of fourfold oblation, known by the names of Saprathas and Prathas.
2These sages found what lay remote and hidden, the sacrifice's loftiest secret essence. From radiant Dhatar, Savitar, and Vishṇu, from Agni, Bharadvâja brought the Br̥ihat.
3They found with mental eyes the earliest Yajus, a pathway to the Gods, that had descended. From radiant Dhitar, Savitar, and Vishṇu, from Sûrya did these sages bring the Gharma.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 152r (OPenn image 151, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.180.3 ‹vāmam ojo 'jāyathā vṛṣabha›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 152v, begins in RV 10.182.1 ‹nayatu durgahā tiraḥ punar›. Verses 10.181.1-3 end on this page.
